# BSV facts

Every fact file from `content/facts/`, each under its title with the date it was last verified.

## Arcade broadcaster

verified: 2026-10-22

Arcade is the broadcaster and transaction-status service for BSV. It replaces mAPI and the legacy ARC API: apps submit transactions to Arcade and ask Arcade what happened to them. Public instances need no API key. Hosts per network are listed in the `networks` facts.

### Endpoints

| Call | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `POST /tx` | Submit one transaction. `Content-Type` is one of `text/plain` (hex; surrounding whitespace is trimmed), `application/octet-stream` (raw bytes) or `application/json` with body `{rawTx}` (hex). The transaction may be plain (raw) or Extended Format (BRC-30). BEEF (BRC-62) is rejected: convert it to EF before submitting. `@bsv/sdk` produces EF with `tx.toHexEF()` when every input carries its `sourceTransaction`. Body cap 32 MiB. |
| `POST /txs` | Submit a batch: raw transactions concatenated in one `application/octet-stream` body, no separators. Body cap 256 MiB. |
| `GET /tx/{txid}` | Current status of a transaction this instance has been given. |
| `GET /policy` | Fee rate and size limits that intake enforces (see Policy). |
| `GET /health` | Liveness, Arcade version, current block height and the datahubs it is using. |
| `GET /events?callbackToken=` | Server-Sent Events stream of status updates for every transaction submitted with that `X-CallbackToken`. Served by Arcade's standalone `sse` service, not the main API; on a self-hosted Arcade it listens on its own port (default 8082). Sends `: keepalive` every 15 s; reconnect with `Last-Event-ID` to replay what you missed. |

Optional headers on `POST /tx` and `POST /txs`:

| Header | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `X-CallbackUrl` | Public HTTPS URL that Arcade POSTs `TransactionStatus` bodies to as the transaction progresses. Private and loopback hosts are refused. |
| `X-CallbackToken` | Opaque token. Sent back as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` on every webhook, and scopes the SSE stream above. |
| `X-FullStatusUpdates` | `true` delivers every status transition; the default delivers only terminal or notable ones. |

Callbacks or SSE replace polling. Polling `GET /tx/{txid}` with a per-request timeout and a bounded schedule is the fallback.

### Status lifecycle

`txStatus` takes one of twelve values:

| Value | Meaning for an app |
| --- | --- |
| `UNKNOWN` | Non-final. Not a verdict; read again. |
| `RECEIVED` | Arcade has it. Not yet on the network. |
| `SENT_TO_NETWORK` | Forwarded to nodes. Wait. |
| `ACCEPTED_BY_NETWORK` | A node accepted it. Still wait: this is one step short of the gate. |
| `SEEN_ON_NETWORK` | Seen across the network. **Safe to treat as final (0-conf)** when `competingTxs` is absent or empty. |
| `SEEN_MULTIPLE_NODES` | Later than `SEEN_ON_NETWORK`; same rule. |
| `DOUBLE_SPEND_ATTEMPTED` | Terminal. Another transaction spends the same input; `competingTxs` names it. |
| `REJECTED` | Terminal. `extraInfo` carries the reason and `status` the ARC code when classifiable. |
| `PENDING_RETRY` | Non-final. Arcade is retrying the broadcast (`retryCount`, `nextRetryAt`). |
| `STUMP_PROCESSING` | Arcade is assembling the block proof (a STUMP, a subtree merkle path). Past the gate. |
| `MINED` | In a block; `blockHash`, `blockHeight` and `merklePath` (BUMP, hex) are set. Never wait for this before treating a payment as final. |
| `IMMUTABLE` | Deep enough that a reorg is no longer expected. |

The single gate for every money decision: `SEEN_ON_NETWORK` or later, with no competing transaction. Earlier statuses wait; `REJECTED` and `DOUBLE_SPEND_ATTEMPTED` are terminal; `UNKNOWN` and `PENDING_RETRY` are non-final, never "dead".

A `REJECTED` reason that starts `parent rejected` names a rejected ancestor and is retryable: resubmit once the ancestor is accepted. A reason that blames inputs (`UTXO_SPENT`, `missingorspent`, "already spent") on a transaction the network had already accepted usually means it was mined or spent by itself; treat it as no verdict and read again.

### Response shapes

`POST /tx` answers:

- **202** `{txid, status, txStatus}`: `status` is the HTTP code (202) and `txStatus` the lifecycle state. A resubmission of a known txid also answers 202 and echoes the current state, which may already be `MINED`, `REJECTED` or `DOUBLE_SPEND_ATTEMPTED`. A 2xx is provisional: always read `GET /tx/{txid}` afterwards.
- **400** `{error, reason?, txid?, status?, title?, detail?, type?}`: `status` is the numeric ARC code when the failure is classifiable, with its `title`, `detail` and documentation URL `type`. A validator failure is terminal and persisted as `REJECTED`. The exception is 476 (not final), which is transient and not persisted.
- **503** with `Retry-After`: backpressure. The transaction was not queued; retrying is safe.

`GET /tx/{txid}` answers 200 with a `TransactionStatus`, or 404 when this instance has no verdict for the txid.

| `TransactionStatus` field | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| `txid`, `txStatus`, `timestamp` | Always present. |
| `status` | Numeric ARC code (460–476) recorded with a `REJECTED` verdict when classifiable; omitted otherwise. |
| `extraInfo` | Free-form detail, such as the node's rejection reason. |
| `competingTxs` | Array of conflicting txids. Omitted when there are none. |
| `blockHash`, `blockHeight`, `merklePath` | Set from `MINED` on. A mined transaction whose proof is momentarily unavailable still returns `MINED` with `merklePath` omitted; read again. |
| `rawTx` | Hex of the transaction as Arcade holds it, in Extended Format. The OpenAPI file documents it as set "only while PENDING_RETRY"; it was observed on `MINED` transactions on testnet on 2026-10-22. Do not depend on it being present. When it is, re-read it as a plain transaction (`Transaction.fromHex(Transaction.fromHexEF(hex).toHex())`) before putting it in a BEEF: the EF form carries placeholder parents. |
| `retryCount`, `nextRetryAt` | Broadcast retry state. |
| `orphanedProofs` | Earlier block anchors superseded by a reorg, if any. |
| `callbacks` | Webhook delivery state, only when the request carries `?callbackToken=`. |

### ARC codes

| Code | Meaning | Handling |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 460 | Not Extended Format (a parent's output data is needed) | Attach `sourceTransaction` to every input and submit EF. |
| 461 | Malformed transaction or invalid unlocking script | Terminal. Fix the transaction. |
| 465 | Fee too low | Terminal for those bytes. Re-size the fee from the serialized transaction at the current `/policy` rate. |
| 466 | Conflicting transaction (`UTXO_SPENT`) | Terminal, unless the conflicting transaction is your own earlier copy. |
| 476 | Not final (nLockTime ahead of median-time-past with a non-final input) | Transient. Nothing is persisted and `GET /tx/{txid}` keeps its prior answer (404 on a first submission). Resubmit the identical transaction after the lock time passes. |

### Policy

`GET /policy` returns `{policy: {miningFee: {satoshis, bytes}, maxtxsizepolicy, maxscriptsizepolicy, maxtxsigopscountspolicy, standardFormatSupported}, timestamp}`. It always answers 200 and reflects what intake enforces.

| Network | `miningFee` | `maxtxsizepolicy` | `maxscriptsizepolicy` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| testnet (`arcade-testnet-us-1`) | 1 sat / 1000 bytes | 100000000 | 100000000 |
| mainnet (`arcade-us-1`) | 100 sat / 1000 bytes | 100000000 | 100000000 |

On mainnet every datahub Arcade reported in `/health` advertised 100 sat/kB. Arcade's size limits track the largest limit any peer advertises, and some individual peers advertised a `maxscriptsizepolicy` of 500000 or 10000000. A script larger than 500 KB may pass Arcade yet reach fewer nodes; test it on testnet first. `maxtxsigopscountspolicy` 4294967295 means unlimited.

### Observed timing

Measured on testnet, Oct 2026:

- `GET /tx/{txid}` returned a status 0.5–2 s after the POST in every one of 19 large broadcasts, and never 404 for a transaction that had been posted.
- `SEEN_ON_NETWORK` arrived within 3–10 s of the POST.
- Arcade can answer 2xx to the POST and mark the transaction `REJECTED` about 20 ms later (seen as ARC 466 `UTXO_SPENT` with the competitor named). The POST answer alone proves nothing.
- A 404 means this instance never saw the transaction, including one a user's wallet broadcast through another service. Submit every transaction you care about to your own Arcade (submission is idempotent) so you can track it.
- Arcade has no address or outpoint index. Address listings and "who spent this outpoint" still need an indexer (see the `whatsonchain` facts).

### Version

Every public instance reported `v0.16.0` in `GET /health` on 2026-10-22. The API is described by `openapi/arcade.openapi.yaml` in `bsv-blockchain/arcade` (OpenAPI `info.version` 1.0.0). `@bsv/sdk` 3.2.1 has no built-in Arcade broadcaster; write a small one around `POST /tx` and `GET /tx/{txid}`. The SDK's `ARC` class posts to the legacy ARC path, which Arcade does not serve, so never use it with Arcade.

## Consensus and policy facts

verified: 2026-10-22

BSV restored the original protocol at the Genesis upgrade. Several Bitcoin habits do not apply.

### Sequence numbers and lock times

- Post-Genesis, `nSequence` is only a finality flag: an input with `nSequence < 0xffffffff` makes `nLockTime` count. There is no transaction replacement, and a higher sequence number does not replace an earlier version on the network.
- BIP68 and `OP_CHECKSEQUENCEVERIFY` are NOPs. There are no relative lock times. `OP_CHECKLOCKTIMEVERIFY` is a NOP too; lock-time logic in script reads `nLockTime` from the transaction preimage.
- `nLockTime < 500000000` is a block height; otherwise it is a Unix time compared with median-time-past (MTP). MTP lags the wall clock by up to about an hour, so a time-locked transaction becomes valid up to an hour after its nominal time.
- A script that gates on a height must also assert `nLockTime < 500000000`, or a timestamp passes the check.
- Arcade answers a not-yet-final transaction with ARC code 476 and keeps no record of it. Resubmit the identical transaction once it is final.

### Opcodes and digests

- There is no `OP_CHECKDATASIG` (that is Bitcoin Cash). A signature over arbitrary data in script needs a Rabin signature (`verifyRabinSig`), or a covenant that reads the spending transaction. Script-level ECDSA costs about 1 MB of script, over the default script-size policy.
- Chronicle activated on mainnet at height 943816 (2026-04-07). It adds opcodes and a sighash flag, and relaxes malleability rules for transactions with version greater than 1. Stay on version-1 transactions and BIP-143 sighash digests unless you specifically need Chronicle features.

### Default node policy

| Policy | Default |
| --- | --- |
| `maxscriptsizepolicy` | 500000 bytes |
| `maxtxsizepolicy` | 10 MB |
| Script numbers | up to 750000 bytes |

Arcade's `/policy` reports what it enforces, which can be larger (see the `arcade` facts). Individual nodes may still apply these defaults.

### Txid malleability

A txid covers the unlocking scripts. When several parties sign one transaction, the last signer can produce a second valid transaction with the same inputs and outputs and a different txid (a twin). Another party's `SIGHASH_ALL` signature fixes inputs and outputs, not the other scriptSigs. Bind protocol state to "the transaction that spends coin X", not to a txid you saw before every signature was in.

## Fee rates and measured costs

verified: 2026-10-22

### Rates

| Network | Minimum Arcade accepts | Rate to configure |
| --- | --- | --- |
| testnet | 1 sat/kB | 100 sat/kB, so testnet sizes and costs carry over to mainnet |
| mainnet | 100 sat/kB on every datahub Arcade reports | 100 sat/kB |

100 sat/kB is also the default rate of BSV Desktop and `@bsv/wallet-toolbox`. Read `GET /policy` on your Arcade before relying on any number here; rates are set by the network and can change.

### Measured sizes and costs

Measured on testnet, Oct 2026, paying 100 sat/kB. Sizes are serialized transaction bytes.

| Transaction | Size | Fee |
| --- | --- | --- |
| P2PKH funding transaction from a BRC-100 wallet | 225–965 B | 23–97 sats |
| Opening that creates a 9.6 KB covenant output (two funding inputs) | 10042–10340 B | 1005–1034 sats |
| Stateful covenant transition (spends the covenant and recreates it with new state) | 29436–29439 B | 2944–2945 sats |
| Covenant close paying out to two parties | 19509–19620 B | about 1970 sats |
| Small P2PKH refund or withdrawal | 191–328 B | 20–33 sats |

A stateful covenant transition carries the covenant script three times (see the `runar` facts), which is why it is roughly three times the script size.

### Rules

- Size every fee from the serialized draft transaction at the configured rate, never from a guess. An estimate that assumed a few hundred bytes for a transaction carrying a 9.6 KB output made every real submission fail.
- Wallet payout outputs carry at least 546 sats (the dust threshold for outputs a wallet will track). Token outputs by convention hold 1 sat; that is separate from this rule.
- Server-built change under about 50 sats is cheaper to give to the fee than to track.
- Cap fees only where an overpay would harm a counterparty. A cap that a correctly sized transaction can exceed blocks honest use and protects nobody.

## Networks and endpoints

verified: 2026-10-22

Build and test on testnet. Mainnet is real money: switch to it only by explicit configuration (one `BSV_NETWORK` variable read by both server and client), and refuse money paths when the user's wallet reports a different network.

| | testnet | mainnet |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Arcade default | `https://arcade-testnet-us-1.bsvblockchain.tech` (live and used for testnet work, though not listed on the public Arcade docs page) | `https://arcade-us-1.bsvblockchain.tech` |
| Arcade alternates | `https://arcade-v2-testnet-us-1.bsvblockchain.tech` | `https://arcade-eu-1.bsvblockchain.tech`, `https://arcade-ap-1.bsvblockchain.tech`, `https://arcade-v2-us-1.bsvblockchain.tech`; also `https://arcade.gorillapool.io` (listed in the Arcade docs, not in `versions.json`) |
| WhatsOnChain API base | `https://api.whatsonchain.com/v1/bsv/test` | `https://api.whatsonchain.com/v1/bsv/main` |
| Explorer | `https://test.whatsonchain.com` | `https://whatsonchain.com` |
| Getting coins | Faucet `https://bsvfaucet.com`: sign in with a BSV wallet, up to 10M sats per request, 24 h cooldown | Buy BSV; there is no faucet |
| Fee reality | Arcade minimum 1 sat/kB | 100 sat/kB on every datahub Arcade reports |
| `getNetwork()` (`@bsv/sdk` BRC-100 wallet) returns | `'testnet'` | `'mainnet'` |
| `@bsv/wallet-toolbox` `Chain` | `'test'` | `'main'` |

The `Chain` type in `@bsv/wallet-toolbox` 2.14.9 also has `'stn'`, `'ttn'`, `'tstn'` and `'mock'`; apps use only `'test'` and `'main'`. `@bsv/simple` 0.7.0 has a third spelling, `'testnet' | 'main'` (see the `@bsv/simple` gotchas).

The hosts above are the ones in `content/versions.json` (`services.arcade.hosts`), all live at `v0.16.0` on 2026-10-22. The `arcade-v2-*` hosts are the ones hardcoded in `@bsv/wallet-toolbox`'s network configuration.

### Local wallet

BSV Desktop, the reference BRC-100 desktop wallet, serves the wallet interface locally on HTTP port **3321** and HTTPS port **2121**; `WalletClient('auto', originator)` finds it. A local BSV Desktop is often set to mainnet: read `getNetwork()` before any money path.

### ttn

`https://arcade-v2-ttn-us-1.bsvblockchain.tech` serves a Teranode test network. It is neither testnet nor mainnet: coins, blocks and txids there do not exist on either. Use it only when you mean to, as an explicit Arcade URL; tools in this kit accept it only that way and warn.

## Payment channels

verified: 2026-10-23

What a payment channel can and cannot be on BSV today, for an app that broadcasts through Arcade. Measurements marked "testnet, Oct 2026" were verified on testnet in BSVA's earlier apps, Oct 2026.

### What a channel is on BSV

Two parties lock funds in one output, then pass signed transactions that spend it back and forth off-chain, each one updating the balance or the shared state. Only the last version is broadcast. If one party stops answering, the funds come back to the other after a fixed time.

The Bitcoin SV wiki page `https://wiki.bitcoinsv.io/index.php/Payment_Channels` (read 2026-10-23) defines the channel transaction as one with `nSequence < 0xffffffff` and an `nLockTime` in the future, updated between the peers until the lock time arrives or the sequence is made final. It names three ways to manage a channel:

1. "In public via mining network."
2. "In private with pre-funded UTXO per channel."
3. "In private with separate channels for content purchase and service delivery per user."

Only the two private options work for an app built with this kit; the reason is in "Who holds a non-final transaction today" below.

### Sequence numbers, lock times and finality

- A transaction is final at once when every input has `nSequence == 0xffffffff`, or when `nLockTime == 0`.
- Otherwise it is final only when `nLockTime` is strictly less than the comparison value of the block that would mine it: the block height when `nLockTime < 500000000`, the median-time-past (MTP) otherwise. A transaction with `nLockTime = H` can be mined from block `H + 1`.
- MTP lags the wall clock by up to about an hour, so a lock time in seconds matures up to an hour late.
- There are no relative lock times: BIP68 and `OP_CHECKSEQUENCEVERIFY` are NOPs.
- Consensus has no replacement rule. A higher `nSequence` does not replace an earlier version; once the lock time has passed, every signed version that spends the outpoint is equally valid. Nodes keep the first version they see and refuse later conflicting ones (first-seen is node policy); consensus accepts whichever version is mined.

Sources: the `consensus` facts; `util/lock_time.go` in `bsv-blockchain/teranode` (`https://github.com/bsv-blockchain/teranode/blob/main/util/lock_time.go`, read 2026-10-23), whose comment says the strict inequality matches SV Node's `IsFinalTx`.

### Who holds a non-final transaction today

| Service | What it does with a non-final transaction | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Arcade | Answers `POST /tx` with 400 and ARC code 476, and persists no verdict. `GET /tx/{txid}` keeps answering 404 after a submission that only ever got 476. Resubmit the identical transaction once it is final. Arcade never holds, orders or replaces channel states. | `openapi/arcade.openapi.yaml` in `bsv-blockchain/arcade` (`https://github.com/bsv-blockchain/arcade/blob/main/openapi/arcade.openapi.yaml`, read 2026-10-23); the `arcade` facts; an earlier BSVA design that resubmits every 5 minutes on 476 until the state is accepted (a design constant, not a testnet measurement). |
| Teranode | Rejects it as invalid under the consensus rule its source labels TNJ-13. The same comment says payment channels are for the user to set up and run, and that the node "shouldn't be aware or care about them". | `util/lock_time.go` in `bsv-blockchain/teranode`, read 2026-10-23. Read from source, not probed live. |
| SV Node | Keeps a separate non-final (time-locked) transaction pool. This is node policy, not consensus. Default size 50 MiB; an entry not updated for 4 weeks is dropped; a non-final transaction that spends the output of another non-final one is refused; to change a submitted transaction the participants negotiate a new version. | The BSV hub page `https://hub.bsvblockchain.org/wiki/transactions-and-utxos/bitcoin-transactions/transaction-pools`, read 2026-10-23. **Not verified:** whether nodes relay these transactions to each other; that the replacing version must carry a higher `nSequence` (stated on other hub pages, not re-read); the defaults in current SV Node releases. |

An app that broadcasts through Arcade therefore cannot park a channel state on the network. The parties hold every state themselves, and only final transactions are broadcast.

### Sighash flags a channel uses

| Flag | Name | What the signature commits to | Use in a channel | Binds the channel's value? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `0x41` | ALL\|FORKID | every input and every output | the fee payer's own inputs; a referee's attestation | yes |
| `0xc1` | ALL\|ANYONECANPAY\|FORKID | this input and every output | a balance update between parties with no covenant, with the payer's change output fixed | yes: every output is committed |
| `0xc2` | NONE\|ANYONECANPAY\|FORKID | version, this input's outpoint, scriptCode, value, this input's `nSequence`, and `nLockTime`; no outputs | a signature over a state carried in `nSequence`, which a covenant checks with a plain `OP_CHECKSIG` | no: safe only when a covenant pins outputs that carry the input's whole value, or the input carries no value |
| `0xc3` | SINGLE\|ANYONECANPAY\|FORKID | this input, the output at the same index, and `nLockTime` | a signed record at input 0 and output 0 that lets whoever closes add fee inputs and change at index 1 or later | only that one output: safe when it covers every satoshi of the input, a covenant pins outputs that carry the input's whole value, or the input carries no value (a 1-sat record channel) |

A value split between two parties with no covenant must be signed `0xc1` (or `0x41`). A Rúnar stateful transition does not pin its change output, so the covenant must pin outputs that account for the whole input value before `0xc2` or `0xc3` is safe (see the `runar` facts). With `0xc2` the closer chooses every output; with `0xc3` the closer can add an output that takes whatever the committed output leaves.

The wiki's streaming example asks for a `SIGHASH_ANYONECANPAY | SIGHASH_NONE` signature; on BSV that is `0xc2`, because FORKID is always set.

A signature in script is DER followed by the sighash byte. It must be canonical DER with a low S value. `createSignature({ hashToDirectlySign })` signs the 32 bytes it is given, so pass it the double SHA-256 of the BIP-143 preimage (`TransactionSignature.format` in `@bsv/sdk`, with `scope` set to the flag).

Sources: the BIP-143 digest as implemented by `TransactionSignature.format` in `@bsv/sdk` 3.2.1; testnet, Oct 2026 (`0xc3` and `0xc2` states validated under `@bsv/sdk` `Spend` and mined). `0xc1` is standard BIP-143 and was not used in those apps.

### nSequence as a state carrier

Any `nSequence` below `0xffffffff` keeps `nLockTime` enforced and carries no other meaning, so the field is free space for the channel. An 18-bit game state fitted in it; so did a plain counter of updates. A Rúnar covenant reads it with `extractSequence` and the lock time with `extractLocktime`.

Sources: the `runar` facts; testnet, Oct 2026.

### Ordering states without replacement

With no replacement, the newest state has to become valid first. Two schedules were measured on testnet, Oct 2026:

- **Seconds.** State `n` carries `nLockTime = base − n × 10 s`. Blocks arrive about every 10 minutes and MTP lags, so neighbouring states mature in the same block and the ordering is only nominal. The party that held every state (there, an operator) was the real enforcer.
- **Heights.** State `k` carries `T(k) = openHeight + (9 − k) × W` with `W = 6` blocks. Each state matures a full window before its predecessor, which was enough for each client to defend itself.

A stale state broadcast after the newest one was answered `REJECTED`, ARC 466 `UTXO_SPENT`, with the newer transaction listed in `competingTxs`.

The cooperative close is final (`nSequence 0xffffffff`, `nLockTime 0`) and valid at once.

Source: testnet, Oct 2026.

### Arcade observations for channel transactions

Testnet, Oct 2026:

- A 1-sat channel output and a 0-sat `OP_FALSE OP_RETURN` record output were accepted.
- Chains of unconfirmed covenant spends were accepted and mined together, nine of them in one block.
- Every time-locked covenant transaction (posts, pins, judged closes, claims, the abandon and the refund) was posted once the tip had reached its lock time, read from an indexer first, and none was answered 476.
- `GET /tx/{txid}` answered 0.5–2 s after the POST.
- The opening reached `SEEN_ON_NETWORK` within seconds, and updates started at 0-conf.

Sources: testnet, Oct 2026; the `arcade` facts carry the same timings.

### Sizes and fees

At 100 sat/kB. Sizes are serialized transaction bytes. The covenant and wallet-payment rows were measured on testnet, Oct 2026; the referee rows are design estimates, not measurements.

| Transaction | Size | Fee |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Referee channel: opening with a 1-sat channel output (design estimate) | about 350 B | about 35 sats |
| Referee channel: close carrying a data record (design estimate) | about 400 B fixed + 13.5 B per update, so about 1.5 KB for 80 updates | about 150 sats for 80 updates |
| Covenant channel (9.6 KB script): opening | 10042–10340 B | 1005–1034 sats |
| Covenant channel: a state posted on chain | about 29.4 KB | 2945 sats |
| Covenant channel: close | 19.5–19.6 KB | about 1970 sats |
| Covenant channel: pre-signed refund | 191 B | 20 sats |
| Per-payment alternative: a wallet-built P2PKH payment | 225–965 B | 23–97 sats, one wallet spend each |

In the referee channel the operator pays the opening and the close; the two parties pay nothing. Anchoring the same 80 updates as separate transactions was computed at about 4,300 sats and observed at about 8,000 sats with wallet rounding and change, and cost each party a wallet prompt per update (40 each).

Sources: the `fees` facts carry the same covenant and wallet-payment measurements; the referee estimates and the anchoring figures are from BSVA's earlier apps, Oct 2026 (the anchoring cost observed on testnet).

### What cannot be done on chain

- No transaction can be bounded "not after" a time or height. Lateness is handled by racing the late transaction with a conflicting spend, such as a pre-signed refund.
- Script cannot read the current height. Deadlines are anchored to an opening height that both parties signed, and every height gate also asserts `nLockTime < 500000000`, or a timestamp passes it.
- The last signer of a multi-party transaction can produce a twin with the same inputs and outputs and a different txid. Bind the channel to "the transaction that spends coin X", not to a txid seen before every signature was in (see the `consensus` facts).

Sources: the `consensus` facts; testnet, Oct 2026.

### Wallet facts for channels

- `createSignature({ hashToDirectlySign })` signs exactly the 32 bytes given (the double SHA-256). Under a level-1 protocol covered by a BRC-73 grouped grant it signs without a prompt, one call per state (see the `wallet-limits` facts).
- `@bsv/wallet-toolbox` keeps provided inputs first and, with `randomizeOutputs: false`, keeps outputs in the given order. A state signed by both parties can therefore be published through such a wallet with `createAction`, the signed channel input at index 0; then submit its EF to your own Arcade (see the `arcade` facts). **Not verified:** whether BSV Desktop keeps that order. The fallback is to hand the user the signed state as a file.

Sources: the `wallet-limits` facts; testnet, Oct 2026 (verified with `wallet-toolbox`; publishing through BSV Desktop was not run).

## Rúnar contracts

verified: 2026-10-22

Rúnar compiles TypeScript-style contract classes to Bitcoin Script. Use it for every contract, and take it from upstream source, not npm.

### Version state

| Source | Version | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| npm `runar-sdk` (and siblings) | 0.4.6 | Stale and unsafe. Its stateless `checkPreimage` is forgeable. Never use it. |
| `icellan/runar` branch `main` | commit `d207ee8` (2026-09-18), packages at `1.0.0-rc.1` | Use this. No release or tag exists for 1.0 (tags stop at `v0.4.6`), and there were no newer commits on 2026-10-22. |

Pin the commit, vendor the built packages, and commit the compiled contract artifact.

### Build recipe

1. Install pnpm (the repo uses pnpm workspaces and turbo).
2. Clone `https://github.com/icellan/runar`, check out `main` at the pinned commit.
3. `pnpm install` and `pnpm build` at the repo root.
4. `pnpm pack` each package you need (`runar-lang`, `runar-compiler`, `runar-ir-schema`, `runar-sdk`, `runar-testing`). Packing rewrites their `workspace:*` dependencies to real versions.
5. Copy the tarballs into your repo (for example `vendor/runar/`) and point every `runar-*` name at them with `pnpm.overrides` in the root `package.json`, so no copy resolves from npm.
6. Add `fast-check` to your own dependencies if you use `runar-testing`: it is declared there only as a dev dependency.

Record the commit and the rebuild steps next to the tarballs.

### 1.0.0-rc.1 behaviour to know

- Give a private method's result a typed local before doing arithmetic on it.
- Only bounded `for` loops compile, and each iteration is unrolled into the script. Unbounded loops, recursion and closures are rejected.
- The compiler caps the stack at 800 items.
- `this.buildP2PKH` is documented but missing in rc.1; build P2PKH outputs another way.
- Each public method has a fixed set of outputs. Plan methods around the exact outputs they create.
- A stateful state transition carries the contract script three times: in the preimage's script code, in the code part pushed by the unlocking script, and in the recreated output. Size fees accordingly (see the `fees` facts).
- `StatefulSmartContract` in rc.1 has a sound OP_PUSH_TX binding, and `addOutput` pins the continuation amount. `_changePKH` and `_changeAmount` are chosen by the spender and are not pinned unless a signature covers the outputs. A terminal method that pays out must pin its outputs itself: `hash256(serializedOutputs) == extractOutputHash(txPreimage)`.
- `extractLocktime` returns the raw field. Every height check must also assert `nLockTime < 500000000`.
- `TestContract` in `runar-testing` mocks `checkSig`. Test signature and preimage behaviour with real transactions through `@bsv/sdk` `Spend`.
- The SDK's `call()` cannot add fee inputs or payout outputs. Build settlement transactions with `@bsv/sdk` and Rúnar's `buildUnlockingScript` (stateless) or its `encodeArg` / `encodePushData` / `encodeScriptNumber` helpers in the stateful layout `<codePart> <args…> <_changePKH> <_changeAmount> <preimage> <methodIndex>`. Never hand-assemble unlocking scripts.

### Browser builds

`runar-ir-schema` calls `fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)`, which crashes every browser page that imports it. In Vite, alias `node:url`, `node:path` and `node:fs` to browser shims, and add a build check that fails when any unshimmed Node builtin reaches the bundle.

Ship a slim artifact to the browser: `script`, `abi`, `stateFields`, `constructorSlots`, `codeSeparator` and `version`. The full compiler output inlines about 1 MB of source maps.

### Rabin signatures

BSV script has no data-signature opcode, so a signature over arbitrary data is checked with `verifyRabinSig` (about 50 bytes of script). The check is

`(sig² + padding) mod n == LE_uint256(SHA256(msg))`

where `LE_uint256` reads the 32-byte digest as a little-endian unsigned integer and the public modulus `n` must be larger than 2^256. BRC-100 wallets sign ECDSA only, so a Rabin key lives outside the standard wallet calls unless the wallet has a Rabin module (BRC-206, draft).

## 1Color tokens (BRC-162, BRC-207)

verified: 2026-10-22

1Color is the fungible token standard for BSV apps: BRC-162 defines the output format, BRC-207 the wallet module that holds and spends it. 1Color is the binary encoding of the BSV-21 token model; BRC-161 is the JSON-inscription encoding of the same model, and a token's id is shared across both.

### BRC-162 output layout

Every token output's locking script starts with a prefix that is pushed and then dropped, so any script can follow it:

```
<token id | OP_0> <amount | OP_0> OP_2DROP [<payload> OP_DROP] <rest of the locking script>
```

- **Token id**: the outpoint of the token's deploy output. On the wire it is the deploy txid as 32 bytes in internal byte order (deploys under BRC-162 are always output 0). A 36-byte form (txid plus little-endian vout) exists only for tokens first deployed under BRC-161 at a non-zero output. For display and APIs the id is `<txid>_<vout>`, for example `<64 hex>_0`.
- **Amount**: a minimally encoded script number, 1 to 2^64 − 1 for value. Zero (`OP_0`) marks authority, not an empty balance.
- **Payload** (optional): one push followed by `OP_DROP`. Fields are read only when it is a strictly valid DAG-CBOR map. Deploy-only display fields are `sym` (symbol, not unique), `icon` (`[mediaType, bytes]`) and `dec` (decimals 0–18, display only). Reserved keys `req` and `ext` declare wallet processing profiles; `req` is fixed at deploy.
- **Rest**: any valid locking script (P2PKH, multisig, a covenant). There is no protocol tag: the layout is the marker.

### Roles and operations

| Token id | Amount | Role |
| --- | --- | --- |
| empty | > 0 | Deploy, fixed supply: the whole supply in this output |
| empty | 0 | Deploy, authority supply: the first minting authority |
| present | 0 | Authority: may mint, split, combine, transfer or end |
| present | > 0 | Value: a spendable balance |

- **Deploy** is valid only at output 0. That output's outpoint becomes the token id.
- **Transfer**: value outputs are admitted only when the sum of the token's value inputs covers them. If outputs exceed inputs, the outputs are invalid and the inputs are burned. If inputs exceed outputs, the difference is burned.
- **Mint**: spending a valid authority lets the transaction create value outputs without covering inputs.
- **Burn**: give up value by not recreating it (explicit or implicit).
- **Authority** outputs can be split, combined, re-locked to a new owner, or ended. Minting stops only when no authority output remains.

Validity is enforced by indexers and overlays, not by miners. Always key tokens by deploy outpoint, never by symbol.

**1 sat convention:** token outputs usually hold 1 satoshi. That is ecosystem practice, not a protocol rule; BRC-207 services admit valid outputs whatever their satoshi value.

### BRC-207 wallet flow

The `color` wallet module works through the existing BRC-100 calls:

- **Keys**: each managed output's key is derived like BRC-29, with protocol `[2, "p color <assetTag> <prefixTag> <suffixTag>"]` and `keyID` `color`. `assetTag` is the deploy txid hex, `v`, and the output index (or `issue` for a new deploy); prefix and suffix tags are the hex of the remittance strings' UTF-8 bytes.
- **Baskets**: one value basket `p color <assetTag>` and one authority basket `p color <assetTag> authority` per asset. Read-only `listOutputs` views `p color assets`, `p color balance <assetTag>` and `p color balance <assetTag> authority` give inventory and exact balances.
- **Plans**: an action's intent (assets, owned outputs, operations such as `transfer`, `mint`, `burn`, `deploy-fixed`, `authority-split`, input and change positions) travels as JSON, hex encoded in `labels` of the form `p color plan <partIndex> <partCount> <hexChunk>`, at most 200 hex characters per chunk. Burns and authority operations must be declared explicitly.
- **Signatures**: `createSignature` with the module protocol, `keyID: "color"` and `data` set to a UTF-8 JSON envelope `{version: 1, tx, inputIndex, sighashType, ownedOutputs}` where `tx` is Atomic BEEF bytes; `hashToDirectlySign` must be absent. The wallet computes the digest itself and returns a DER signature.
- **Overlay admission**: per asset, topic `tm_color_<assetId>` and lookup service `ls_color_<assetId>`. Before releasing any spend signature, the wallet checks every token input against the asset's overlay for current spendability, using providers the user has accepted.
- **Receiving**: `internalizeAction` with `basket insertion` into the asset's basket and `customInstructions` `{version: 1, assetId, derivationPrefix, derivationSuffix, senderIdentityKey}`.
- **Discovery**: a wallet with the module may advertise `brc207-color=4` in its version string (BRC-205). Absence does not prove the module is missing.

### Implementation status (2026-10-22)

| Piece | Status |
| --- | --- |
| BRC-162 encoding | `@bsv/templates` 2.0.0 ships `Bsv21Binary`, a script template for the binary prefix. |
| Overlay | `@bsv/overlay-topics` 2.0 (2.0.1 on npm) ships `Bsv21TopicManager` and `Bsv21LookupService` plus a BRC-162 ledger module. The per-asset `tm_color_<assetId>` naming is BRC-207's; check which topic names a host actually serves. |
| BRC-207 wallet module | Only in interim forks under `@bopen-io/*` (for example `@bopen-io/wallet-toolbox` 2.15.1). Not in `@bsv/wallet-toolbox` 2.14.9, and BSV Desktop does not support it yet. |
| BRC-162 "Implementations" section | "None yet". |

### Naming history

Earlier drafts of the binary format were called Mandala Tokens and then Colored Tokens. The original Mandala Token Protocol (BRC-92) is withdrawn. Token ids, scripts and amounts did not change with the rename, and the wallet module does not accept earlier `p mandala` identifiers.

### Scope in this kit

Phase 1 gives encoding guidance only: how to build and read BRC-162 outputs with `Bsv21Binary`, and how ids, roles and balance rules work. Wallet-held 1Color balances wait for BRC-207 to land in `@bsv/wallet-toolbox` and BSV Desktop. `@bsv/simple`'s `createToken` makes PushDrop tokens, which are not 1Color.

## BRC-100 wallet limits and permissions

verified: 2026-10-22

### Client-side result limits

`@bsv/sdk` checks these on the client for every wallet substrate (`WalletClient`, HTTP JSON, `window.CWI`, Wallet Wire). A wallet that answers outside them fails in the app, whatever the wallet itself allows.

| Call | Limit |
| --- | --- |
| `getPublicKey` result | `publicKey` is 33 bytes (66 hex), a valid compressed point |
| `createSignature` result | canonical DER, at most 72 bytes |
| `verifySignature` argument | DER at most 72 bytes, checked before sending |
| `createHmac` result | exactly 32 bytes |
| `encrypt` / `decrypt` results | any byte array up to 256 MiB; the only calls that carry arbitrary bytes |
| `protocolID` | `[0..2, string of 5–400 chars]` in the SDK (the BRC-43 text says 280) |
| `keyID` | 1–800 characters in the SDK (BRC-43 allows up to 1033 bytes) |
| `createSignature` arguments | exactly one of `data` or `hashToDirectlySign`. `hashToDirectlySign` is 32 bytes and must be the **double**-SHA256 digest of what you mean to sign. Sign only digests you rebuilt yourself, never one received over the wire. |

Extending a wallet beyond these limits goes through a BRC-98 `p <scheme>` permission module, not a new method. Such modules bypass the wallet's normal permission manager, so a module must authorize its own requests and must reject `p`-namespace baskets and labels.

### BRC-29 payment derivation

- Protocol ID `[2, '3241645161d8']`.
- `keyID = prefix + ' ' + suffix` (derivation prefix and suffix, base64 strings, joined by one space).
- The sender derives the recipient's key with `counterparty = recipient` (the recipient's identity key).
- The recipient verifies the same key with `counterparty = sender` and `forSelf: true` before signing anything that pays it.
- The recipient collects with `internalizeAction({ protocol: 'wallet payment', paymentRemittance: { senderIdentityKey, derivationPrefix, derivationSuffix } })`.
- Keep derivations deterministic or persisted. A random prefix and suffix that were never saved make the payment unrecoverable.

### Grouped permissions manifest (BRC-73)

The wallet reads `https://{originator}/manifest.json`. Serve the same object under both keys:

- `metanet.groupPermissions` (the current key)
- `babbage.groupPermissions` (the key BSV Desktop reads)

Contents:

- `spendingAuthorization { amount, description }`: `amount` is a **monthly** allowance in sats per originator. There is no duration field. Keep it small.
- `protocolPermissions [{ protocolID, counterparty?, description }]`
- `basketAccess [{ basket, description }]`

Serve it as `application/manifest+json` with open CORS and no caching, ahead of any single-page-app rewrite. Protocol grants do not expire.

### Permission levels

| Level | Scope | Prompt behaviour (BSV Desktop) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | none | never prompts |
| 1 | per originator and protocol | one grouped grant covers every `keyID` and counterparty; use it for anything signed repeatedly |
| 2 | per originator, protocol and counterparty | a manifest entry needs a `counterparty`; without one the wallet prompts once per new peer. Whether `counterparty: 'self'` counts as grouped is unsettled. |

To raise the grouped prompt at "Connect wallet" rather than at the first real action, make one harmless protected call right after reading the identity key, for example `getPublicKey({ protocolID: <your level-1 id>, keyID: 'permissions', counterparty: 'self' })`. Discard the result and never await it in the login path.

### Login

`new WalletClient('auto', originator)` → `waitForAuthentication()` → `getPublicKey({ identityKey: true })` (the user's id) → `getNetwork()`, refusing to continue on a mismatch. In `@bsv/sdk` 3.2.1, `isAuthenticated()` throws on a locked wallet; never use it as a gate.

### Transport limits

- BSV Desktop accepts request bodies up to 50 MB (`express.json({limit:'50mb'})`) and does no extra SDK validation on its server side.
- `@bsv/auth-express-middleware` (BRC-103/104) caps parsed JSON bodies at roughly 100 k nodes, so BEEF sent as a `number[]` is limited to about 100 kB. Send larger BEEFs as `beefHex` strings.

## WhatsOnChain usage limits

verified: 2026-10-22

WhatsOnChain (WoC) is a block explorer and indexer. Arcade answers for any transaction you know the txid of; use WoC only for questions Arcade cannot answer, because Arcade has no address or outpoint index. Base URLs per network are in the `networks` facts.

### Allowed endpoints

| Endpoint | Use it for |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /address/{a}/unspent` | Coins at an address (Arcade has no address index). |
| `GET /tx/{txid}/{vout}/spent` | Who spent an outpoint, including unconfirmed spenders. |
| `GET /chain/info` | Tip height (`blocks`). |
| `GET /tx/{txid}/proof/tsc` | A merkle proof, when you do not already hold one. |
| `GET /tx/{txid}/hex` | Only for a transaction Arcade never saw. For anything you broadcast, ask Arcade, and build BEEF from the BEEFs you already hold. |

Never use WoC as the source of truth for a txid you know, and never walk a transaction's ancestry one parent at a time from WoC.

### Rate limits

- The free tier allows about 3 requests per second per IP; above that WoC answers HTTP 429.
- Route every WoC call in a process through one shared gate that spaces requests at least 350 ms apart, and back off on 429. One gate per process, not one per module.
- An optional `WOC_API_KEY` raises the limit. Send it as the raw value of the `Authorization` header (no `Bearer` prefix).
- Give every call a per-request timeout.

### Traps

- `GET /tx/{txid}/hex` can 404 for a fresh unconfirmed transaction. That means "not indexed yet", not "does not exist".
- `/address/{a}/unspent` keeps listing coins that an unconfirmed transaction has already spent, until that transaction is mined. Expect `UTXO_SPENT` from Arcade if you try to spend one; check `/tx/{txid}/{vout}/spent` first.
- Check that any hex WoC returns hashes to the txid you asked for before you use it.
- WoC indexes an unconfirmed spend 6–12 s after broadcast (measured on testnet, Oct 2026). Arcade reports the same transaction within 0.5–2 s, so gate on Arcade.
